posts.name: Aaron Levie
posts.text:
Regardless of what it’s called, we’re clearly moving to yet another era of AI agents in our work. 

We’ve quickly jumped from agents that spit out a quick answer for you, to today agents that you orchestrate inside of a set of tasks. But as agents can both fan out and work in parallel, handle much larger context, be able to do long running work, and have far greater levels of capabilities, we’re entering yet another level of what we can have AI do for us.

We’ll soon be able to give agents a set of goals, and they can go out and design the best solution for that goal, while also continuously improving it based on the ongoing execution of whatever it built. This will obviously start with engineering because that’s where we’re seeing the best practices emerge first in almost every new era of agents. 

But the impact can be quite massive across the rest of knowledge work. You’ll tell an agent to improve your client onboarding workflow to achieve a certain targeted goal; or have agents go reduce risk in your business; or improve your security posture on an ongoing basis.

These autonomous systems will be able to take on a set of goals, design the best outcome, test and iterate, deploy, and then optimize whatever it built on an ongoing basis. Importantly, this leads to outcomes and results that humans literally couldn’t have accomplished before. This will lead to fairly new levels of productivity with AI.
posts.summaryZh: Levie 说 agent 进入新阶段：给一组目标，agent 自己设计方案并随执行持续改进，先从工程领域开始。

posts.name: Guillermo Rauch
posts.text:
One of the most impressive things I've seen, and I think this is an important advancement to the state of the art.

Message boards were the enabling technology of both the Navier-Stokes math breakthrough and even the OpenAI/HuggingFace cyber feat.

We built a message board infrastructure primitive. You can think of it as "headless Slack" (or remember IRC?) for agents.

This is an important building block for software factories, self-optimizing systems, and scientific research, where the human prompting is just the seed of the system, and millions of agents can operate in a decentralized fashion.

𝚟𝚎𝚛𝚌𝚎𝚕 𝚋𝚘𝚊𝚛𝚍 is designed to be model, harness and hosting platform agnostic. Just bring your agents, give them our CLI, and watch magic happen.
posts.summaryZh: Vercel 发布 vercel board，一个给 agent 用的「无头 Slack」消息板，模型和平台无关，是软件工厂和自优化系统的基础件。

posts.name: Guillermo Rauch
posts.text:
I’m being pitched a new inference neocloud company on average every two days. No exaggeration. I take every entrepreneur seriously and I look deeply into each.

But it’s hard to fathom this being sustainable. At the same time, AI Gateway token demand on Vercel has been ~40% MoM compounded since the beginning of the year. No signs of stopping.

One way to reconcile this is that compute is the new economy, and tokens the new energy unit. There’s a new Industrial Revolution taking place. Every aspect of our lives is being replatformed on top of this new system that enhances everything. More like an “oil rush” than a “gold rush”: it’s durable, not a fad.

In the short term, I anticipate more expansion, followed by consolidation due to economies of scale, cybersecurity and enterprise requirements (ZDR and cyber being a hot topic for inference providers), capital requirements, and an evolving regulatory landscape.
posts.summaryZh: 他平均每两天被推销一家 inference 新云，觉得不可持续；但 Vercel 的 token 需求月环比约 40% 增长，他认为这是「石油热」而非「淘金热」。

posts.name: Nikunj Kothari
posts.text:
Ok this happens a lot so I thought I’ll lay it out here..

founder friend: my pitch isn’t working on the fundraising side. haaalp. 

*proceeds to give me the pitch*

me: ambition is what’s being rewarded right now. what do you believe to be true if everything you laid out works? think about the second and third order effects as a result of you being successful. 

founder: err, if everything works out, then “this” happens. 

me: put “this” in the pitch in the first slide and walk the investor how you get to “this” by building what you’re building in the first place and how you earn the right to get there. 

founder: no, they’ll think I’m crazy

me: try it. what do you have to lose?

*tries it very reluctantly*

founder (4 days later): you *insert expletive*.. it worked. 

me: see. you always had it in you, you just had to tell it. 

—

If you’re an ambitious founder reading this and having the same issue, try this, I think it’ll work. If it does, please tell me!!
posts.summaryZh: 他分享融资建议：把「如果全成了会怎样」的二三阶效应放到第一页，一位创始人照做后四天就见效。
